description: 4yo boy with color blindness; pedigree shows X-linked pattern. X-linked recessive: males with one mutant X allele are affected; females are carriers. Color blindness is a classic X-linked recessive disorder.

11mo with seizures, pale skin, blue eyes, musty-smelling urine — PKU. Pleiotropy = one gene mutation causing multiple unrelated phenotypic effects. Single PAH defect causes intellectual disability, seizures, hypopigmentation, and musty odor.

5yo boy with behavioral problems, hyperphagia, almond-shaped eyes, cryptorchidism. Prader-Willi: deletion/methylation of paternal chr 15q or maternal UPD15. Methylation of maternal chromosome 15 silences the only remaining copy.

15yo boy with learning disability, hyperactivity, poor social skills, increased CGG repeats (FMR1 gene). Features: long face, large everted ears, macroorchidism, autism spectrum disorder. Most common inherited intellectual disability.

topic: Primary ciliary dyskinesia — dynein arm defect
description: 31yo man with chronic respiratory infections, infertility, situs inversus (dextrocardia on CT). Kartagener/PCD: autosomal recessive defect in dynein arms → immotile cilia → bronchiectasis, sinusitis, situs inversus, male infertility.

2720g female newborn with micrognathia, prominent occiput, low-set ears, clenched fists with overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom feet, VSD. Second most common trisomy. Second trimester quad screen: ↓AFP, ↓estriol, ↓hCG.

48yo alcoholic man with burn injury, develops confusion, agitation, horizontal nystagmus, broad-based gait. Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) is cofactor for transketolase/pyruvate dehydrogenase. Glucose given without thiamine first worsens Wernicke.

7mo male with fatigue, weakness, failure to thrive, enlarged tongue, crackles, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on X-ray. Pompe: deficiency of lysosomal acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase) → glycogen accumulates. Pompe 'pumps' the heart.

34yo man with carcinoid syndrome (palpitations, wheezing, flushing, diarrhea, ↑urinary 5-HIAA), on octreotide; new drug added. Telotristat inhibits tryptophan hydroxylase — rate-limiting step in serotonin synthesis — to control refractory diarrhea.

61yo woman with UTI treated with fluoroquinolones. Fluoroquinolones cleave DNA to relieve supercoils by inhibiting DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV in bacteria, preventing DNA replication.

9yo boy from Northern Canada with diffuse bone pain, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia; bone marrow biopsy shows lipid-filled macrophages resembling crumpled tissue paper. Gaucher: deficiency of β-glucocerebrosidase → glucocerebroside accumulates.

5yo boy with easy bruising, velvety/fragile skin that stretches further than normal, joint hypermobility, increased range of motion. Ehlers-Danlos: defective collagen cross-linking due to impaired lysine/hydroxylysine cross-linking by lysyl oxidase.

46yo man with T2DM, insulin glargine added. Table shows effects on glycolysis/glycogenesis/lipolysis/gluconeogenesis. Row B correctly shows insulin's anabolic effects: ↑glycolysis, ↑glycogenesis, ↓lipolysis, ↓gluconeogenesis.

55yo strict vegan with pale oral mucosa, ↓vibration sense in lower extremities, hypersegmented neutrophils on blood smear (macrocytic anemia). B12 is cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and methionine synthase. Deficiency → subacute combined degeneration.

9yo girl with recurrent URIs, renal polyps, short stature, epiphyseal widening on wrist X-ray; lab table. Row A (↓Ca, ↓PO4, ↑PTH, ↓calcitriol) is consistent with vitamin D deficiency causing rickets/osteomalacia.

36yo woman with RA on methotrexate, elevated AST/ALT. Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP/B6) is the essential cofactor for aminotransferases (AST and ALT). Methotrexate can deplete folate but PLP is required for transaminase function.

Investigator studies muscle biopsy from 82yo woman with sciatic nerve injury showing shrunken cells with dense eosinophilic cytoplasm, nuclear shrinkage, plasma membrane blebbing (apoptosis). Intrinsic pathway: BAX/BAD release cytochrome c from mitochondria → activates caspases.

77yo man with HTN, T2DM, AF found dead; spleen shows pale region with preserved cellular architecture and pyknotic nuclei — splenic infarction. Coagulative necrosis: ischemic cell death in solid organs; architecture preserved, pyknotic nuclei remain.

16yo girl on dapsone for leprosy, with lethargy/headache, chocolate-colored blood on venous sampling; ABG table. Methemoglobinemia: Fe3+ cannot bind O2. Row C shows elevated MetHb with normal PaO2 but ↓O2 saturation.

38yo man with emphysema/COPD (1 pack/day, 20 years), flattened diaphragm, increased radiolucency; cells elaborating elastase entered by chemotaxis. LTB4 is the most potent chemotactic factor for neutrophil recruitment to sites of inflammation.

30yo man, 1 month after chemical burn on right hand/forearm; thick contracted scar, restricted wrist range of motion. Wound contraction is mediated by myofibroblasts (proliferative stage, days 3-7). Excessive proliferation causes pathologic contracture.

22yo woman with painful swelling of left foot after stepping on rock; localized erythematous, fluctuant lesion. Mast cell degranulation → histamine release → separation of endothelial junctions → ↑vascular permeability → local edema.

32yo Somali immigrant with fever, cough, weight loss, bilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy; biopsy shows multinucleated Langhans giant cells in caseating granulomas. Granulomas = fused epithelioid macrophages stimulated by IFN-γ from Th1 cells.

topic: IL-2 — activates NK and cytotoxic T cells
description: 71yo woman with metastatic melanoma treated with aldesleukin (IL-2); investigator studies mechanism. IL-2 stimulates NK cells and cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, which recognize absence of MHC I on tumor cells → cell-mediated tumor killing.

69yo woman with hemoptysis, weight loss, cavitary right lung lesion, squamous cell carcinoma on biopsy; which finding confers worst prognosis? Mediastinal invasion = T4 in TNM classification. Staging (spread) determines prognosis more than grade.

35yo woman, father died of colon cancer at 42, endometrial carcinoma, MLH1 germline mutation. Lynch syndrome (HNPCC): DNA mismatch repair gene mutations → instability of short tandem DNA repeats (microsatellites) → increased cancer risk.

33yo woman with prior osteosarcoma, father died of adrenocortical carcinoma at 41, now breast adenocarcinoma. Li-Fraumeni: autosomal dominant TP53 mutation → multiple malignancies at early age (osteosarcoma, breast cancer, brain tumors, adrenocortical carcinoma).

72yo man with progressive lower extremity weakness, urinary incontinence, back pain, osteoblastic lesions on spine X-ray; metastatic prostate cancer with spinal cord compression. PSA (prostate-specific antigen) is elevated in metastatic prostate cancer.

42yo woman with urge incontinence (involuntary leakage with sudden need to void), failed conservative therapy. Oxybutynin antagonizes muscarinic M3 receptors in bladder detrusor muscle → ↓bladder contraction → ↓urgency and frequency.

6yo boy with enuresis, desmopressin initiated; mechanism of action of desmopressin (V2 receptor). Desmopressin binds V2 receptor → Gs → adenylyl cyclase → ↑cAMP → ↑aquaporin-2 insertion in collecting duct → ↑water reabsorption.

Investigator studying drug B with existing drug A; dose-response graph shows rightward shift of curve with same maximum efficacy. Competitive antagonist: shifts curve right (↓potency), same Vmax (efficacy unchanged); overcome by increasing agonist concentration.

Novel enzyme study; test serum shows ↑Vmax, unchanged Km compared to control. Increased enzyme concentration → ↑Vmax (more active sites available), no change in Km (substrate affinity is intrinsic property of enzyme, not amount).

56yo man with coronary artery disease, isosorbide mononitrate given orally and IV; no statistically significant difference in dose-corrected AUC. Identical AUC for oral vs IV = 100% bioavailability. Isosorbide mononitrate does not undergo significant first-pass metabolism.

Research group conducts trial with 20 volunteers to estimate maximum tolerated dose and monitor apparent toxicity. Phase I trial: first-in-human, small group of healthy volunteers, evaluates safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics.

64yo woman with AF on warfarin, prescribed griseofulvin, develops subtherapeutic INR. Griseofulvin is a CYP450 inducer → ↑warfarin metabolism → ↓warfarin serum levels → ↓anticoagulation effect → subtherapeutic INR.

2yo boy with recurrent bacterial infections; flow cytometry shows abnormal NADPH oxidase activity; susceptible to catalase-positive organisms. CGD: defective NADPH oxidase → ↓reactive oxygen species → cannot kill catalase-positive bacteria (S. aureus, Serratia, Aspergillus, Nocardia).

39yo HIV+ man (CD4 520), pneumonia, alpha-hemolytic organism on blood agar. S. pneumoniae's polysaccharide capsule is its primary virulence factor — prevents opsonization by masking surface antigens from antibodies and complement-mediated lysis.

55yo woman with T2DM and sepsis; blood/sputum grow gram-negative, catalase-positive, encapsulated bacilli (P. aeruginosa). Lipid A (component of LPS on gram-negative outer membrane) → activates macrophages/complement → TNF-α, IL-1 → vasodilation → hypotension/septic shock.

7yo unvaccinated boy with low-grade fever, paroxysmal cough, whooping sound, post-tussive emesis, lymphocytosis. Pertussis toxin: ADP-ribosylates Gi → disinhibits adenylyl cyclase → ↑cAMP → impairs neutrophil recruitment and immune signaling.

23yo man in crowded conditions with 2-week dry cough, fatigue, myalgias; mobile skin discoloration of fingers/toes (Raynaud), papular lesion on extremities. Mycoplasma pneumoniae: atypical pneumonia with cold agglutinins; no cell wall so gram stain negative.

27yo man with nausea/vomiting 30 minutes after eating reheated rice at a barbecue; symptoms resolve next morning. B. cereus food poisoning: preformed cereulide (emetic toxin) in reheated starchy food → rapid onset vomiting within 30 min-6 hours.

35yo man with painless penile chancre and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy; darkfield microscopy shows gram-negative spirochetes (T. pallidum). Penicillin G: first-line treatment; inhibits transpeptidase (PBP) → blocks peptidoglycan cross-linking → bacterial cell wall lysis.

57yo man with generalized malaise, jaundice, pruritic rash on dorsum of hands (porphyria cutanea tarda), anti-HCV positive; not seen physician in 15 years. HCV is primarily transmitted parenterally (needlestick injury, injection drug use, blood transfusion pre-1992).

49yo homeless man diagnosed with HIV 25 years ago, never received ART, no symptoms; homozygous mutation that prevents HIV entry into macrophages. CCR5 is the coreceptor used by HIV for macrophage entry; homozygous CCR5Δ32 deletion confers near-complete resistance.

26yo HIV+ man with CD4 count 162/mm3; most appropriate prophylaxis. TMP-SMX (Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis) is indicated when CD4 <200/mm3. Most common opportunistic infection in HIV patients without prophylaxis.

28yo HIV+ primigravida at 38 weeks; zidovudine started to reduce perinatal transmission. Zidovudine (AZT): NRTI — nucleoside analog lacking 3'-OH group → chain termination of reverse transcriptase → prevents elongation of viral DNA.

31yo man returning from vacation with 2-day abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea; photomicrograph shows trophozoite with ingested RBCs. E. histolytica: trophozoites ingest RBCs — pathognomonic finding. Diagnose with stool O&P. Treat: metronidazole + paromomycin.

44yo male with periodic high fevers, malaise; recurrent episodes after travel to Africa; blood smear shows ring forms. Plasmodium falciparum: most virulent species causing malaria, no exoerythrocytic phase (no hypnozoites like vivax/ovale). Treat with artemisinin-based therapy.

41yo man with papular skin lesions, oral mucosa lesions; India ink prep shows encapsulated yeast. Cryptococcus neoformans: encapsulated yeast diagnosed by India ink or latex agglutination. Causes meningitis in AIDS (CD4 <100). Treat: amphotericin B + flucytosine.

21yo woman with 5-day foul-smelling vaginal discharge, dysuria, vaginal burning; wet mount prep shows motile flagellated protozoa. T. vaginalis: sexually transmitted, pH >4.5, frothy yellow-green discharge, strawberry cervix. Treat both partners with metronidazole.

65yo healthy man compared to adolescent; which immune changes occur? Aging causes ↓naive T and B cells, ↓affinity maturation, ↓V(D)J recombination → decreased responsiveness to new antigens (vaccines). Total immunoglobulin levels remain normal.

topic: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis — T cell defect
description: 21yo woman with recurrent white tongue plaques and nail fungal infections; KOH shows budding yeasts with pseudohyphae. Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis: impaired T cell response to Candida antigens due to STAT1 gain-of-function or AIRE protein defects → defective IL-17 signaling.

21yo man with dyspnea, hemoptysis, hematuria, blood-tinged sputum; anti-GBM antibodies positive. Goodpasture: anti-GBM antibodies (IgG against type IV collagen) → type II hypersensitivity → pulmonary-renal syndrome. Linear IgG deposits on GBM immunofluorescence.

23yo man with cadaveric renal transplant 4 days ago; rising creatinine, tubulitis on biopsy, C4d staining negative. Acute cellular rejection: T lymphocyte-mediated (allorecognition → T cell activation). C4d negative indicates cellular not humoral rejection.

7yo unvaccinated boy with trismus, opisthotonos, autonomic hyperactivity; which vaccine type prevents this? Tetanus toxoid = denatured bacterial product (inactivated exotoxin) → induces active immunity without causing disease.

3mo boy with recurrent infections, delayed umbilical cord separation, leukocytosis; flow cytometry shows absent CD18. LAD type 1: autosomal recessive defect in CD18 (β2-integrin) → neutrophils cannot migrate to infection sites. Recurrent infections, absent pus formation.

2yo boy with recurrent Neisseria infections; serum CH50 inappropriately low. Terminal complement deficiency (C5-C9): cannot form membrane attack complex → predisposes to recurrent Neisseria bacteremia (N. meningitidis, N. gonorrhoeae).

17yo girl with 3-week sore throat, fever, lymphadenopathy, fatigue; heterophile antibody test positive. EBV complication: Hodgkin lymphoma (via LMP1 activation of NF-kB). Also associated with Burkitt lymphoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

48yo woman with heart transplant, hypertension, gingival hyperplasia; side effects from immunosuppressant. Cyclosporine: binds cyclophilin → inhibits calcineurin → prevents NFAT dephosphorylation → ↓IL-2 transcription → ↓T cell activation. Side effects: nephrotoxicity, HTN, gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism.

39yo man on isoniazid for TB with fatigue, dyspnea, microcytic anemia; bone marrow shows blue-ringed sideroblasts. Isoniazid inhibits B6 (pyridoxine) → ↓ALA synthase activity → defective heme synthesis → iron trapped in mitochondria of RBC precursors (ringed sideroblasts).

3yo boy with abdominal pain, constipation, delayed verbal development; peripheral blood smear shows small pale red cells with basophilic stippling. Lead inhibits ALA dehydratase (conversion of ALA to porphobilinogen) and ferrochelatase → defective heme synthesis → microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling.

topic: Hemolytic disease of newborn — ABO incompatibility
description: One-day-old female newborn with jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, reticulocytosis; mother type O, infant type A; no prenatal care. ABO incompatibility: natural anti-A IgG crosses placenta → hemolysis; can occur in 1st pregnancy unlike Rh incompatibility.

8yo Asian girl with microcytic anemia, normal hemoglobin electrophoresis, normal serum ferritin; peripheral smear shows small pale RBCs. Cis deletion of alpha-globin genes (--/αα): common in Asians. Two-gene deletion → mild microcytic anemia with normal Hgb electrophoresis and normal ferritin.

9yo African American boy with painful shoulder swelling, recurrent bone pain, fever after soccer; peripheral blood smear. Howell-Jolly bodies (nuclear remnants in RBCs) appear due to functional asplenia in sickle cell disease. Autosplenectomy from repeated vaso-occlusive infarctions.

34yo man with blurry vision, headache, ↑RBC/WBC/platelets, ↓EPO. PV: JAK2 V617F gain-of-function mutation (nonreceptor tyrosine kinase) → EPO-independent myeloid cell proliferation → erythrocytosis, thrombocytosis, leukocytosis.

55yo man with fatigue, recurrent bleeding; bone marrow biopsy shows leukemic cells with t(15;17) translocation and Auer rods. AML (acute myeloid leukemia): myeloperoxidase (MPO) stain positive; distinguishes from ALL. t(15;17) = APL → treat with ATRA.

Previously healthy 68yo woman with nausea, anorexia, polyuria, confusion, progressive back pain; ↑ESR, ↑Ca, ↑creatinine, ↑protein on SPEP. Multiple myeloma: malignant plasma cells secrete osteoclast activating factors (TNF-α, IL-1, RANKL) → lytic bone lesions → hypercalcemia.

10yo boy with profuse bloody diarrhea; petechiae on trunk/extremities, ↑creatinine, peripheral smear shows schistocytes. HUS: Row A = normal PT/PTT, ↓platelets, ↑BUN/Cr, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia — distinct from DIC which has abnormal coagulation.

9yo boy with painful knee swelling after soccer, prolonged bleeding following tooth extraction; ↑PTT, normal PT, normal bleeding time. Hemophilia impairs intrinsic pathway → conversion of factor X by the intrinsic pathway is impaired. Factor Xa can still form via extrinsic pathway (factor VII).

66yo man with AF; warfarin initiated for long-term embolic stroke prevention. Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase → ↓γ-carboxylation of glutamate residues on coagulation factors II, VII, IX, X (and proteins C, S) → inactive coagulation factors.

28yo man with testicular swelling; biopsy shows mixed germ cell tumor with invasion of adjacent lymphatic vessels. Testicular cancer spreads via lymphatics to para-aortic (retroperitoneal) lymph nodes — embryological origin near mesonephros. NOT inguinal nodes (those drain the scrotum).

57yo man with CHF, EF 39%; new drug decreases serum renin and angiotensin II concentrations. Beta-1 receptor blockade in juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney → ↓renin release → ↓angiotensin II → ↓aldosterone → ↓preload/afterload. Classic mechanism of beta blockers in heart failure.

2850g newborn with small, retracted mandible and zygomatic bone hypoplasia. The incus derives from the 1st branchial arch (along with malleus, mandible, muscles of mastication). First arch = Meckel's cartilage. Pierre Robin sequence and Treacher Collins are 1st arch anomalies.

topic: Persistent truncus arteriosus — neural crest failure
description: 5-day-old boy with cyanosis, poor feeding; echocardiography shows single great vessel. Persistent truncus arteriosus: failure of neural crest cell migration → incomplete aorticopulmonary septum formation → single outflow vessel receiving output from both ventricles. Associated with DiGeorge syndrome.

topic: Tetralogy of Fallot — right axis deviation on ECG
description: 6mo girl with episodic cyanosis relieved by squatting ('tet spells'). Right axis deviation on ECG is due to right ventricular hypertrophy (compensatory from RVOTO). TOF: VSD, overriding aorta, pulmonary stenosis, RVH. Boot-shaped heart on CXR.

30yo man with Down syndrome, fatigue, digital clubbing; right atrial pressure 32 mmHg. Eisenmenger: uncorrected left-to-right shunt (AV canal defect in Down syndrome) → pulmonary HTN → ↑RV pressure → RV remodeling and right ventricular hypertrophy → shunt reversal → cyanosis.

topic: Cor pulmonale — increased capillary hydrostatic pressure
description: 63yo woman with sleep apnea, shortness of breath on exertion, right bundle branch block, bilateral pitting ankle edema. Cor pulmonale: pulmonary HTN from sleep apnea → RV failure → ↑RV filling pressure → ↑capillary hydrostatic pressure → ↑Starling forces → peripheral edema.

27yo man shot in abdomen, BP 88/65 mmHg, free fluid in abdomen; hemodynamic table. Hypovolemic (hemorrhagic) shock: Row B = ↓CO (↓preload), ↓PCWP (↓LV filling), ↑SVR (compensatory vasoconstriction). Distinguish from cardiogenic (↑PCWP) and distributive (↓SVR) shock.

32yo Colombian man with 3-month shortness of breath, fatigue; LV pressure-volume curve shows ↓compliance (diastolic dysfunction). Cardiac sarcoidosis: noncaseating granulomas → restrictive CMP with preserved EF. Also causes conduction abnormalities and arrhythmias.

30yo woman from China with worsening fatigue/dyspnea; loud S1 on examination. S1 = mitral and tricuspid valve closure at the onset of systole. Loud S1 is classically heard in mitral stenosis (mobile but thickened leaflets snap shut with greater velocity).

topic: S3 heart sound — increased LV end-systolic volume
description: 72yo woman with worsening shortness of breath, lower extremity swelling, weight gain; early diastolic sound at 5th left intercostal space. S3 gallop: rapid blood decelerates hitting distended ventricle during early filling. Caused by ↑LV end-systolic volume (ventricular volume overload) in systolic heart failure.

60yo man with prior STEMI 3 weeks ago with new fever, pleuritic chest pain, high-pitched scratching sound, pericardial effusion. Dressler syndrome (2-10 weeks post-MI): autoimmune response to cardiac antigens released from necrotic myocardium → immune complex-mediated pericarditis.

47yo woman with fever, weight loss, cardiac murmur, ↑creatinine, red cell casts and protein on urinalysis; mitral valve vegetations at autopsy. IE-related GN: antigen-antibody complex deposition in glomeruli → complement activation → classic pathway GN with renal failure.

topic: Wolff-Parkinson-White — slurred upstroke of QRS (delta wave)
description: 23yo man with AF and palpitations; verapamil given, patient becomes unresponsive; autopsy shows accessory atrioventricular conduction pathway (Bundle of Kent). WPW: ventricular pre-excitation → slurred upstroke (delta wave) + short PR interval. Avoid AV nodal blockers in WPW with AF.

58yo man with diffuse muscle pain, weight loss, arthralgia, skin lesions; renal findings; biopsy shows transmural inflammation of arterial wall with fibrinoid necrosis. PAN: medium-vessel vasculitis; absence of p-ANCA; associated with hepatitis B; spares lungs; no glomerulonephritis.

13mo boy with hepatosplenomegaly; venous blood sample is milky; apolipoprotein C-II gene mutation. Familial hyperchylomicronemia (Type I dyslipidemia): LPL or apoC-II deficiency → ↑↑chylomicrons/TG → recurrent acute pancreatitis, eruptive xanthomas, lipemia retinalis.

topic: Statin adverse effects — elevated creatine kinase
description: 62yo woman with HTN and T2DM prescribed a statin for primary prevention; most likely adverse effect. Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → ↓CoQ10 → impaired mitochondrial energy production in muscle → myalgia, muscle weakness, ↑CK. Risk of rhabdomyolysis, especially with fibrates or niacin.

topic: Superior laryngeal nerve — voice pitch limitation
description: 38yo woman undergoes hemithyroidectomy for papillary thyroid carcinoma; splenic lobe directly adjacent to superior thyroid artery dissected. External branch of superior laryngeal nerve innervates cricothyroid muscle → voice pitch limitation (inability to produce high-pitched sounds) if damaged during thyroid surgery.

34yo woman with 3-month fatigue, weight loss despite eating more; ↑heart rate, warm moist skin, proptosis bilaterally. Graves disease: TSH receptor autoantibodies (TRAbs) stimulate TSH receptor → hyperthyroidism + diffuse goiter + exophthalmos (proptosis). Associated with HLA-DR3/B8.

28yo woman gravida 1 at 10 weeks; thyroid function tests table. Row A: ↑TBG (estrogen stimulates liver synthesis), ↑total T3/T4, normal free T3/T4, normal TSH. Patient is clinically euthyroid. Same pattern occurs with oral contraceptive use.

71yo homeless man with severe muscle cramps, back pain; ↓Ca, ↑phosphate, ↑creatinine; X-ray shows alternating sclerotic and radiolucent bands in vertebral bodies (rugger jersey spine). Secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD: ↓renal 1α-hydroxylase → ↓calcitriol → ↓Ca → ↑PTH → renal osteodystrophy.

37yo man, 2 days after emergency laparotomy, ↑thirst, polyuria; serum Na 151 mEq/L, urine osmolality 110 mOsm/kg; changes resolved after desmopressin. Central DI: damage to posterior pituitary → ↓ADH secretion. Desmopressin reverses central (not nephrogenic) DI.

Previously healthy 2yo boy with unsteady gait, bilateral saccadic eye movements (opsoclonus-myoclonus), nontender abdominal mass. Neuroblastoma: small blue cells arranged in rosettes around a central neuropil (Homer-Wright rosettes). Most common extracranial solid tumor in children. ↑urinary VMA/HVA.

33yo man with 5-month fatigue, weight loss, orthostatic hypotension, hyperpigmentation, vitiligo; lab table. Row F (↓Na, ↑K, ↑BUN, ↓glucose) = Addison disease: ↓cortisol, ↓aldosterone → hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia, hyperpigmentation (↑ACTH/MSH).

53yo man with fatigue, recurrent diarrhea, 8 kg weight loss; scaly lesions in different phases of healing around mouth/perineum (necrolytic migratory erythema); solid mass in upper abdomen. Glucagonoma: functional neuroendocrine tumor of pancreatic α-cells → ↑glucagon → diabetes, NME, DVT, diarrhea.

59yo man with 6-month numbness/burning in feet (diabetic neuropathy); HbA1c 10.2%. T2DM pathophysiology: peripheral insulin resistance + ↑demand → ↑production of proinsulin and amylin → accumulation of islet amyloid polypeptide (proamylin) in pancreatic islets → β-cell toxicity.

topic: Cushing syndrome — small cell lung cancer (ectopic ACTH)
description: 41yo woman with irregular menstrual cycles, hirsutism, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis; ↑serum/urine cortisol not suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone. Ectopic ACTH from small cell lung cancer: ACTH resistant to negative feedback; elevated ACTH and cortisol not suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone.

44yo man with increased urination, ↑thirst, darkened skin, diabetes mellitus signs; biopsy shows periportal hepatocytes with brownish-yellow iron deposits. Hemochromatosis: HFE gene mutation → defective binding of transferrin to its receptors → ↑iron reabsorption → accumulation in liver, pancreas, skin, heart.

27yo man with pheochromocytoma symptoms, mucosal neuromas on tongue, marfanoid habitus, firm thyroid nodule (likely medullary thyroid cancer). MEN 2 (A and B): gain-of-function RET proto-oncogene mutation → medullary thyroid carcinoma + pheochromocytoma. MEN 2B also has mucosal neuromas and marfanoid habitus.

35yo woman with palpitations, diarrhea, weight loss, ↑T3/T4; TSH-producing pituitary adenoma (secondary hyperthyroidism). TSH binds G protein-coupled receptor on thyroid cells → Gs → adenylyl cyclase → ↑cAMP AND Gq → phospholipase C → ↑IP3/DAG → thyroid hormone synthesis.

Pharmacology question on mechanism of sulfonylureas for T2DM. Sulfonylureas (glipizide, glyburide) block ATP-sensitive K+ channels in pancreatic β-cells → membrane depolarization → Ca2+ influx → insulin secretion. Glucose-independent mechanism → risk of hypoglycemia.

topic: Chagas disease — absence of myenteric plexus neurons
description: Patient with dysphagia and achalasia-like presentation after travel to South America. Trypanosoma cruzi (Chagas): destroys myenteric (Auerbach's) plexus neurons → achalasia (esophagus) and megacolon. Also causes dilated cardiomyopathy. Vector: Triatoma (reduviid 'kissing bug').

Patient with hematemesis following forceful retching/vomiting. Mallory-Weiss: mucosal (not transmural) lacerations at gastroesophageal junction from forceful vomiting. Presents with hematemesis after retching. Associated with alcohol use, bulimia. Most stop bleeding spontaneously.

Patient with peptic ulcer disease and H. pylori infection. H. pylori (gram-negative microaerophilic rod) is the strongest risk factor for PUD. Urease enzyme neutralizes gastric acid → bacterial survival. Diagnose: urea breath test, stool antigen. Treat: triple therapy (PPI + amoxicillin + clarithromycin).

Patient with diarrhea, weight loss, arthralgias, cardiac symptoms; PAS-positive foamy macrophages in small bowel lamina propria. Tropheryma whipplei: gram-positive intracellular bacilli; PAS-positive granules in macrophages are pathognomonic. Treat: TMP-SMX for 1 year.

topic: Hirschsprung disease — impaired neural crest migration
description: Neonate with failure to pass meconium, abdominal distension; rectal biopsy shows absent ganglion cells. Hirschsprung: failure of neural crest cells to migrate to distal colon → absent myenteric and submucosal plexuses → functional obstruction. Treat: surgical pull-through.

Patient with terminal ileum inflammation, skip lesions, transmural involvement, non-caseating granulomas; Th1 activity elevated. Crohn disease: Th1-mediated chronic transmural inflammation; any part of GI tract (terminal ileum most common); cobblestone mucosa, fistulas, strictures.

topic: Portal hypertension — superior epigastric vein (caput medusae)
description: Patient with cirrhosis and visible dilated abdominal wall veins. Portal HTN → portosystemic shunts including caput medusae: retrograde flow from portal to superior epigastric veins → dilated abdominal wall veins. Other shunts: esophageal varices, hemorrhoids.

topic: Hepatitis B serology — chronic active infection
description: Hepatitis B serology table. Row E: HBsAg+, anti-HBs−, anti-HBc+ (IgG), HBeAg+ = chronic active hepatitis B with active viral replication. HBeAg positivity indicates active replication and high infectivity. Treat with tenofovir or entecavir.

Patient with RUQ pain, fever, leukocytosis, positive Murphy sign. Acute cholecystitis: gallstone impacted in cystic duct → gallbladder distension → inflammation → RUQ pain, fever, ↑WBC. HIDA scan: delayed/absent gallbladder visualization. Treat: cholecystectomy.

Patient with progressive jaundice, weight loss, vague abdominal pain radiating to back; pancreatic head mass. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma of the head: obstructive jaundice (painless), Courvoisier sign, Trousseau syndrome (migratory thrombophlebitis). ↑CA 19-9. High mortality.

Congenital infection with cataracts, sensorineural deafness, patent ductus arteriosus findings. Rubella: congenital infection from maternal rubella during pregnancy; transmitted vertically. Classic triad: cataracts, sensorineural deafness, congenital heart disease. Prevent with MMR vaccine.

Patient with hypopigmented/hyperpigmented macules on trunk; KOH shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. Tinea versicolor: Malassezia globosa (normal skin flora, dimorphic yeast) → hypopigmented or hyperpigmented non-scaling patches. Treat: selenium sulfide shampoo or topical azoles.

Patient with flaccid skin blisters and mucosal ulcers; positive Nikolsky sign; biopsy shows intraepidermal vesicle with tombstone pattern. Pemphigus vulgaris: IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein (desmosome proteins) → acantholysis → flaccid blisters. Treat: systemic steroids, rituximab.

Patient with pearly papule with rolled border and central ulceration on sun-exposed skin; palisading nuclei on biopsy. BCC: most common skin cancer; rarely metastasizes; associated with UV exposure, arsenic, Gorlin syndrome (PTCH1 mutation). Treat: Mohs surgery or excision.

Patient on antipsychotic develops hyperthermia, severe muscle rigidity, autonomic instability, altered consciousness, ↑CK. NMS: dopamine D2 receptor blockade → muscle rigidity. Dantrolene: blocks ryanodine receptor → ↓Ca2+ release from sarcoplasmic reticulum → ↓muscle contraction → relieves rigidity.

topic: Myasthenia gravis — decreased end plate potential
description: Patient with fatigable muscle weakness, ptosis, diplopia; positive Tensilon (edrophonium) test; thymoma on chest imaging. MG: autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic ACh receptors → ↓end plate potential → impaired neuromuscular transmission → fatigable weakness worse with activity.

Patient on SSRI prescribed sumatriptan; develops hyperthermia, agitation, hyperreflexia, clonus, diaphoresis. Serotonin syndrome: ↑serotonergic activity from drug combinations. Triptans (5-HT1B/1D agonists) + SSRIs can precipitate serotonin syndrome. Features: clonus, hyperreflexia, hyperthermia (vs NMS: rigidity dominant).

Physiology question on muscle contraction mechanism. Muscle contraction: Ca2+ released from SR → binds troponin C → conformational change in tropomyosin → exposes myosin-binding site on actin → cross-bridge formation → power stroke. Troponin C is the Ca2+-binding subunit that initiates contraction.

Patient with multisystem inflammatory disease; antibody panel shows multiple autoantibody types. Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibodies: highly specific for SLE (~25% sensitive, high specificity). Anti-dsDNA: also specific + correlates with disease activity. ANA: sensitive (~99%) but not specific.

Patient with Raynaud phenomenon, calcinosis cutis, esophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly. CREST syndrome (limited cutaneous SSc): Calcinosis, Raynaud, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasias. Anti-centromere antibodies. Telangiectasias are prominent on face and hands.

Patient with symmetric polyarthritis of small joints, morning stiffness >1 hour, positive RF; synovial biopsy. RA: synovial biopsy shows granulation tissue (pannus) + mononuclear cell infiltrate → pannus invades and destroys articular cartilage and bone at the joint margin.

Patient with sterile arthritis following Chlamydia or enteric infection; urethritis and conjunctivitis also present. Reactive arthritis: HLA-B27 associated; sterile arthritis following GU (Chlamydia) or GI (Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Campylobacter) infection. Classic triad: arthritis + urethritis + conjunctivitis.

Patient with proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash on eyelids, Gottron papules on knuckles; elevated CK. Dermatomyositis: associated with malignancy (ovarian adenocarcinoma most common, also lung, GI, breast). Anti-Mi-2 antibodies. Diagnose: ↑CK, EMG, muscle biopsy.

Patient with bone pain, enlarged skull, hearing loss, bowing of tibia; markedly ↑ALP, normal Ca and phosphate. Paget disease: disordered bone remodeling (↑osteoclast then ↑osteoblast activity) → lamellar bone interspersed with woven bone ('mosaic pattern'). Treat: bisphosphonates.

Patient with contralateral superior homonymous quadrantanopia; MCA stroke territory. Meyer loop: inferior optic radiation fibers in temporal lobe carry superior visual field from contralateral side. Temporal lobe lesion → contralateral superior homonymous quadrantanopia ('pie in the sky').

Smoker with ipsilateral ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis + ipsilateral arm/hand pain; CXR shows apical lung mass. Horner syndrome: interruption of sympathetic chain. Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumor at lung apex → preganglionic Horner syndrome; also compresses C8-T1 → arm/hand weakness and pain.

topic: CN III palsy — posterior communicating artery aneurysm
description: Patient with sudden unilateral ptosis and 'down and out' eye deviation with fixed dilated pupil. CN III palsy with pupil involvement: posterior communicating artery aneurysm compresses oculomotor nerve (parasympathetic fibers on periphery compressed first). Neurosurgical emergency.

Patient with unilateral facial weakness involving both upper and lower face, decreased taste. CN VII exits at cerebellopontine angle → internal acoustic meatus → facial canal → stylomastoid foramen. Vestibular schwannoma at CPA can affect CN VII. Upper AND lower face involvement = peripheral lesion.

topic: Dorsal column tract — vitamin B12 deficiency
description: Patient with progressive weakness, decreased proprioception and vibration sense in lower extremities; prior subtotal gastrectomy. B12 deficiency → subacute combined degeneration: dorsal columns (↓proprioception/vibration) + lateral corticospinal tracts (spastic paresis). Diagnose: ↑methylmalonic acid.

Patient with progressive chorea, personality changes, cognitive decline; family history of similar condition. Huntington: CAG repeat expansion in huntingtin gene (chr 4) → caudate nucleus atrophy → ↓GABA, ↑dopamine. Autosomal dominant with anticipation. Onset 30-50 years. Treat: tetrabenazine for chorea.

Patient with head trauma followed by lucid interval then rapid neurologic deterioration; biconvex hyperdense lesion on CT. Epidural hematoma: rupture of middle meningeal artery (temporal bone fracture) → arterial bleeding between skull and dura. Does NOT cross suture lines. Neurosurgical emergency.

Patient with right leg > arm weakness, urinary incontinence, personality changes; language area spared. Left ACA stroke: contralateral leg > arm weakness (homunculus: leg area is medial), urinary incontinence, transcortical motor aphasia. MCA stroke: face + arm > leg.

Patient with episodic neurologic deficits, optic neuritis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia; CSF shows oligoclonal IgG bands. MS: Th1-mediated autoimmune attack on oligodendrocytes → demyelination of CNS. Relapsing-remitting most common. MRI: periventricular white matter plaques.

Patient with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, NF2 gene mutation; which tumor type is most likely? NF2 (chr 22, merlin protein): bilateral acoustic neuromas (vestibular schwannomas) + meningiomas + ependymomas. Meningiomas arise from arachnoid cap cells (whorled pattern, psammoma bodies).

Patient with spinal cord injury after aortic surgery; bilateral loss of motor function and pain/temperature below lesion with preserved proprioception/vibration. Anterior cord syndrome: injury to anterior 2/3 of spinal cord → bilateral loss of motor (corticospinal) and pain/temperature (spinothalamic); dorsal columns intact.

50yo woman with seizure; MRI shows 4-cm round, sharply demarcated mass; biopsy shows densely packed cells with whorls of lamellated calcification (psammoma bodies). Meningioma: benign tumor derived from arachnoid cap cells of the arachnoid villi. Whorled appearance + psammoma bodies are pathognomonic.

23yo man with excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy (sudden loss of muscle tone with emotion), sleep paralysis, hypnagogic hallucinations. Narcolepsy type 1: autoimmune loss of orexin (hypocretin)-producing neurons in lateral hypothalamus → decreased CSF orexin-A. Treat: modafinil, sodium oxybate.

5yo unvaccinated Nigerian boy with 2-day lower leg weakness, dysphagia, drooling; dies of respiratory failure; autopsy shows destruction of anterior horn cells. Poliovirus destroys anterior horn cells (LMN) → flaccid paralysis, hyporeflexia, muscle atrophy, fasciculations. No sensory loss.

27yo man with ascending progressive weakness and numbness in legs; prior diarrhea; absent patellar reflexes; CSF ↑protein, normal WBC. GBS: post-infectious (Campylobacter most common) autoimmune attack on Schwann cells → peripheral myelin destruction → ascending flaccid paralysis, areflexia.

44yo man with progressive memory loss, personality changes; early onset; history of trisomy 21. Alzheimer disease: extracellular amyloid plaques (Abeta42 from APP cleavage) + intracellular neurofibrillary tangles (tau). APP gene on chr 21 → trisomy 21 patients develop early-onset AD.

topic: Radial nerve palsy — mid-shaft humerus fracture
description: 21yo woman with right arm pain and weakness after MVC; decreased grip strength, marked decrease in wrist extension, mid-shaft humerus fracture on X-ray. Radial nerve injury at mid-shaft humerus → wrist drop, ↓finger extension, ↓sensation over dorsal hand. Patient CAN make a fist (finger flexors intact).

topic: Organophosphate poisoning — muscarinic ACh receptor antagonism
description: 52yo man found on farmland with diaphoresis, miosis, bradycardia, BP 95/60, bronchospasm, fecal/urinary incontinence; clothes soaked with urine/feces. Organophosphate poisoning: irreversible AChE inhibition → ↑ACh → DUMBELS. Treat: atropine (muscarinic antagonist) + pralidoxime (reactivates AChE if given early).

46yo man with alcohol use disorder acknowledges problem but says he lacks 'willpower to cut down.' Transtheoretical model: Contemplation = aware of problem but not yet committed to change. Patient has acknowledged his drinking is a problem but hasn't committed to action or preparation stages yet.

21yo woman with self-harm, recurrent overdoses following breakups, rows of well-healed scars bilaterally on wrists; assaulted paramedic. Splitting is the hallmark defense mechanism of borderline personality disorder: sees people as entirely good or entirely bad; associated with BPD.

26yo man with 6-week history of bizarre delusions, social withdrawal, disorganized speech, and depressed mood. Schizophreniform disorder: same criteria as schizophrenia but duration 1-6 months. About 1/3 recover; 2/3 progress to schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder.

34yo veteran with 2-month difficulty concentrating, fatigue, waking early, ↓appetite, anhedonia (no longer enjoys dancing). MDD: ≥5 SIGECAPS symptoms for ≥2 weeks; must include depressed mood or anhedonia. Treat: SSRIs first-line. Afghanistan deployment 2 years ago suggests PTSD in DDx.

24yo man with forearm wound, 5 jobs in 8 months, imprisoned for credit card fraud, expelled from school at 13 for theft, 6 children with 4 women, doesn't pay child support. ASPD: ≥18 years old + evidence of conduct disorder before age 15; deceitfulness, impulsivity, lack of remorse.

16yo cheerleader with secondary amenorrhea for 4 months, BMI 16.1 kg/m2, pale skin with thin soft body hair (lanugo). Anorexia nervosa complications: severe bone loss due to nutritional deficiencies, ↓estrogen → osteoporosis → stress fractures. Greatest risk complication given her physical activity.

27yo man on new antidepressant, now grandiose, pressured speech, ↓sleep, climbing buildings; previously depressed; seizure disorder. Venlafaxine (SNRI) antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder → precipitates/worsens mania. Must initiate mood stabilizer first; antidepressants alone are contraindicated in bipolar.

28yo man with bipolar disorder on lithium; which parameter should be regularly assessed? TSH: lithium commonly causes hypothyroidism (blocks thyroid iodine uptake) → most common long-term thyroid side effect. Also monitor: creatinine, lithium levels, ECG.

29yo man with schizophrenia on trifluoperazine (high-potency), switched due to akathisia; develops drowsiness, blurred vision, dry mouth. Chlorpromazine: low-potency typical antipsychotic → more anticholinergic (dry mouth, blurred vision) and antihistaminergic (sedation) effects; fewer EPS than high-potency agents.

55yo man post-uncomplicated total knee replacement develops anxiety/agitation, hand tremors, nausea; drinks 7 cups of beer daily. Alcohol withdrawal: first-line treatment with benzodiazepines. In liver disease, use lorazepam/oxazepam/temazepam (LOT) — not hepatically metabolized.

34yo woman with 2-hour increased thirst, erratic behavior, euphoria, diaphoresis, HR 114, BP 156/102; serum sodium 130 mEq/L. MDMA: releases serotonin, dopamine, NE → euphoria, hyperthermia, tachycardia, diaphoresis, hyponatremia (SIADH + ↑water intake). Can precipitate serotonin syndrome with SSRIs.

topic: Acute tubular necrosis — tubular basement membrane denudation
description: 84yo man with decreased urinary output, not drinking for 3 days; serum creatinine 3.1 mg/dL, BUN 42 mg/dL; urinalysis shows multiple brownish granular casts. ATN: ischemic or toxic injury → denudation of tubular basement membrane → free renal tubular epithelial cells slough → 'muddy brown' granular casts.

21yo man found near highway, covering his ears; pH initially 7.47 then 7.38 three hours later; serum ABG table shows mixed acid-base. Salicylate toxicity: initially stimulates respiratory center → respiratory alkalosis, then uncouples oxidative phosphorylation → metabolic acidosis. Result: mixed respiratory alkalosis + high anion gap metabolic acidosis.

topic: Renal tubular physiology — H+/K+ antiporter in alpha-intercalated cells
description: 32yo woman with T1DM, hypokalemia, T-wave flattening on ECG. Hypokalemia from insulin administration → ↑aldosterone → ↑H+/K+ ATPase activity in alpha-intercalated cells of collecting tubule → ↑H+ secretion + ↑K+ reabsorption to correct hypokalemia.

71yo man on furosemide for CHF; serum creatinine 4.8 mg/dL, BUN 48 mg/dL; urine osmolality 600 mOsm/kg, urine sodium 10 mEq/L. Prerenal AKI: ↓renal perfusion from volume depletion (furosemide → fluid loss). BUN:Cr >20:1, FENa <1%, concentrated urine → kidney intact, conserving Na/water.

13yo boy with swelling around eyes, gross hematuria, BP 138/97 mmHg, proteinuria; treated for bacterial tonsillitis 3 weeks ago. PSGN: granular ('lumpy-bumpy') IgG + IgM + C3 deposits on immunofluorescence. Type III hypersensitivity (immune complex deposition). ↓C3, normal C4.

62yo man with T2DM; kidney biopsy shows thickened hyaline arterial wall. Diabetes mellitus causes non-enzymatic protein glycosylation → hyaline arteriolosclerosis of the glomerular arterioles → ↑glomerular capillary pressure → hyperfiltration → progressive nephropathy → Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules.

32yo woman with recurrent UTI, left flank pain; left-sided hydronephrosis; rectangular prisms (coffin lid appearance) on photomicrograph. Struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate) stones: urease-producing bacteria (Proteus, Klebsiella) → ↑NH3 + alkaline urine → struvite precipitation. Can form staghorn calculi.

25yo sexually active young woman with burning urination, urinary frequency; negative nitrite test; urine culture grows organisms resistant to novobiocin. S. saprophyticus: coagulase-negative, novobiocin-resistant gram-positive coccus; second most common cause of UTI in young sexually active women (after E. coli).

72yo multiparous woman with involuntary urine leakage when laughing or sneezing; insulin-dependent T2DM; sensation intact. Stress urinary incontinence: urethral hypermobility from weakened pelvic floor (multiparity, postmenopausal estrogen loss, obesity) → ↑intra-abdominal pressure exceeds urethral resistance → urine leakage.

75yo man on thiazide diuretic with osteoporosis, develops acute gout attack; negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals in synovial fluid; kidney diagram. Thiazides act on distal convoluted tubule (DCT): block Na+/Cl- cotransporter → ↓NaCl reabsorption, ↑Ca2+ reabsorption, ↑uric acid (gout risk).

32yo pregnant woman on carbamazepine for seizure disorder; positive pregnancy test. Carbamazepine inhibits folate absorption → neural tube defects (meningocele/spina bifida) in fetus. Other antiepileptic teratogens: valproate (NTD, highest risk), phenytoin (fetal hydantoin). All epileptics need folate supplementation.

3-day-old female neonate with generalized convulsions, lethargy, poor feeding; posterior uveitis; cranial ultrasound shows ventricular dilation and periventricular calcifications. Congenital toxoplasmosis: classic triad = chorioretinitis + hydrocephalus + intracranial calcifications. Treat: pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine.

1mo girl with bilious vomiting; intestinal malrotation and volvulus; cystic mass behind umbilicus with mature columnar epithelium with goblet cells. Vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct: normally obliterates by week 7. Persistence → Meckel diverticulum or retroumbilical cyst with intestinal mucosa.

2yo girl who can run but cannot walk up/down stairs; scribbles and feeds herself with spoon but cannot dress herself; knows 6 words but cannot combine two words; displays selfish behavior. Row D matches 2-year-old milestones with expected language delay (should combine 2 words by 2 years).

28yo woman with 3-month amenorrhea, acne, hirsutism, nodules along jaw; obese. PCOS: chronic anovulation → unopposed estrogen (no progesterone from corpus luteum) → endometrial hyperplasia → ↑risk of endometrial adenocarcinoma. Most at-risk complication for this patient.

47yo woman with irregular menses, night sweats, insomnia, vulvovaginal atrophy; last menstrual period 2 months ago; quit smoking 2 years ago. Menopause: ovarian failure → ↓estrogen + ↓inhibin B → loss of negative feedback → ↑FSH (most reliable lab marker), ↑LH. FSH >40 IU/L confirms menopause.

8yo girl with short stature, webbed neck, widely spaced nipples, short fourth metacarpals bilaterally; increased risk for which complication? Turner syndrome (45,X): cardiovascular anomalies — bicuspid aortic valve (most common) → premature calcification → aortic stenosis; coarctation of aorta.

Repeated question (same as #171). Turner syndrome (45,X): bicuspid aortic valve is the most common cardiac defect → predisposes to premature aortic stenosis. Patients need echocardiogram surveillance. Associated risk of aortic dissection. Short stature from single SHOX gene copy.

17yo girl brought because she has not had her menstrual period; born with ambiguous genitalia; broke distal radius after minor trauma; multiple ovarian cysts; severe acne. Aromatase (CYP19A1) deficiency: ↑androgens, ↓estrogens → 46,XX: ambiguous genitalia at birth, primary amenorrhea, ovarian cysts, tall stature, osteoporosis.

topic: Adenomyosis — endometrial tissue in uterine wall
description: 39yo woman, gravida 4, with 5-month heavy menses, tender uniformly enlarged uterus consistent with 8-week gestation; menorrhagia and dysmenorrhea. Adenomyosis: endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium → uterine hypertrophy, menorrhagia, dysmenorrhea, uniformly enlarged boggy uterus.

19yo woman with pelvic pain and vaginal discharge for 2 days; pain with cervical motion; Giemsa stain shows intracytoplasmic inclusions (Chlamydia trachomatis). PID (ascending Chlamydia/Neisseria infection) → fallopian tube scarring → ↑risk of ectopic pregnancy and infertility.

4mo male infant with left scrotal swelling; non-tender reducible scrotal mass that transilluminates and increases in size when baby cries. Communicating hydrocele: patent processus vaginalis allows peritoneal fluid into scrotum; increases with ↑intra-abdominal pressure. Usually resolves by 1 year; observe.

Investigator studying influenza-infected vs healthy lung tissue; most likely histopathologic finding. Influenza directly infects and destroys type I pneumocytes (primary alveolar surface cells). Type II pneumocytes (cuboidal, surfactant-producing) proliferate in response to lung damage to replace type I pneumocytes and restore alveolar surface.

32yo man found unconscious on street; respirations slow and shallow; pupils constricted; ABG table shows different acid-base patterns. Row C (↓pH, ↑PCO2, minimal HCO3 compensation) = acute respiratory acidosis consistent with opioid overdose → respiratory depression → CO2 retention. Treat: naloxone.

topic: Severe asthma — physical exam and CXR findings
description: 23yo woman with 2-hour dyspnea; temperature 37.5°C; pulse oximetry 92%; CXR shows hyperinflated lung fields. Severe asthma: Row E = absent breath sounds (severe air trapping), hyperresonance, symmetric chest expansion, ↓tactile fremitus. CXR: hyperinflation, flat diaphragm, wide intercostal spaces.

71yo man with 1-month worsening cough and dyspnea; 1 pack/day smoker for 45 years; autopsy shows cavitating upper lobe lesion. Cigarette smoking = #1 risk factor for lung cancer (especially squamous cell carcinoma and small cell). Cavitating upper lobe lesion = squamous cell carcinoma (central, keratinizing).

62yo woman with progressive dyspnea, dry cough; 1 pack/day smoker for 20 years; FEV1/FVC 65%; ↓DLCO on spirometry. Emphysema: destruction of alveolar walls → ↑lung compliance → air trapping → ↑TLC, ↑RV, ↓FEV1/FVC, ↓DLCO (↓surface area for gas exchange). Centriacinar (smoking): upper lobe predominance.

topic: Cystic fibrosis — absence of vas deferens
description: 15yo boy with recurrent respiratory infections, foul-smelling stools, failure to thrive, nasal polyps, mild wheeze; sweat chloride >60 mEq/L. CF males: bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD) → obstructive azoospermia → infertility. Testicular spermatogenesis intact. >98% of CF males have CBAVD.

topic: Cystic fibrosis — absence of vas deferens (repeated question)
description: Repeated question (same as #182). CF and male infertility: congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens (CBAVD) present in >98% of CF males. Can also occur as isolated finding in men with mild CFTR mutations. CFTR mutation testing recommended in men with obstructive azoospermia.

topic: Sarcoidosis — elevated CD4+ T cells in BAL
description: 30yo woman from Colombia with 3-month shortness of breath, fatigue, facial nodules, anterior uveitis; bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy; ↑ACE. Sarcoidosis: bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) shows elevated CD4+/CD8+ ratio >3.5 (highly suggestive). Non-caseating granulomas. Diagnose: ↑ACE, bilateral hilar adenopathy, tissue biopsy.

70yo man with 4-month progressive dyspnea, dry cough; 1 pack/day smoker for 45 years; on amiodarone; CT shows clustered air spaces and reticular opacities in basal parts of lung. Pulmonary fibrosis: excess collagen deposition by activated fibroblasts → ↓lung compliance → restrictive pattern. Drug-induced from amiodarone.

topic: Pulmonary fibrosis — excess collagen deposition (repeated question)
description: Repeated question (same as #185). Drug-induced ILD/pulmonary fibrosis from amiodarone. Mechanism: direct cytotoxicity + immune-mediated lung injury. Features: dry cough, dyspnea, bibasilar crackles, bilateral reticular opacities. Treat: discontinue amiodarone, systemic steroids.

54yo woman with sharp chest pain, shortness of breath; on raloxifene; HR 92, RR 28/min, PaO2 68 mmHg, O2 sat 92%; ABG shows ↑A-a gradient + respiratory alkalosis. Physical examination most likely shows unilateral leg swelling from DVT — most common source of PE. Diagnose: CT-PA.

13yo boy with recurrent respiratory infections; high-dose fluticasone + salmeterol + oral corticosteroids; new drug added that results in downregulation of FcεRI on mast cells and basophils. Omalizumab: anti-IgE monoclonal antibody that binds free IgE → prevents IgE binding to FcεRI → ↓mast cell/basophil activation → ↓allergic asthma exacerbations.

Investigators conducting prospective cohort study on oral anticoagulants in AF patients with public vs private insurance; 2x2 table. Relative risk (RR) = measure of association in cohort studies. RR = risk in exposed / risk in unexposed = (30/90) / (12/45) = 0.33/0.27 = 1.25 (answer C).

topic: Diagnostic testing — lowering threshold increases NPV
description: Investigators studying Trypanosoma cruzi ELISA; previous cutoff too high; plan to lower threshold by 15%. Lowering diagnostic cutoff: ↑sensitivity (fewer false negatives), ↓specificity (more false positives) → ↓PPV (more false positives), ↑NPV (fewer false negatives → negative test more reliably rules out disease).

Geriatric investigator evaluating consistency of Alzheimer dementia diagnoses by multiple physicians; each evaluator blinded to others' assessments. Precision = reliability = reproducibility. Interrater reliability: agreement between different observers measuring the same subject.

Investigators studying fire retardant chemical and interstitial lung disease; 50 cases and 50 age/geography matched controls; exposure assessed by surveys and home visits. Case-control study: starts with outcome (cases with disease vs controls without), looks backward at exposure; calculates odds ratio; good for rare diseases.

Rheumatologist evaluating hazard ratios from two retrospective cohort studies; Study A: CI 0.89-2, Study B: CI 1.1-2.5 for VTE in RA. Study A CI includes 1.0 → not significant (p>0.05). Study B CI excludes 1.0 → significant (p<0.05). Therefore p-value of Study A > p-value of Study B.

topic: Statistical power — decrease type II error
description: Investigators studying intranasal ketamine for suicidality; pilot study found no significant difference; suspect inadequate statistical power. Statistical power = 1 − beta (type II error rate). To increase power: decrease type II error rate (beta) by increasing sample size or effect size. Most direct way to increase power.

60yo man with painless hematuria; multiple osteolytic spinal lesions; cystoscopy shows 4-cm mass; biopsy shows thickened dysplastic urothelium (transitional cell carcinoma). Cigarette smoking (#1 risk factor for urothelial carcinoma): aromatic amines in tobacco smoke cause DNA damage leading to bladder cancer.

Graduate student studying population with expansive pyramid (high birth rates, low life expectancy). To ensure healthy demographic transition (lower birth + death rates → stable aging population): invest in childhood immunization programs to reduce child mortality and move toward Stage II/III of demographic transition.

4yo girl with sickle cell disease in pain crisis; intranasal fentanyl ordered; mother refuses consent citing fear of morphine addiction. Appropriate response: acknowledge concern, provide factual information about low addiction risk in sickle cell population, and offer information compassionately — respect autonomy while acting in child's best interest.

68yo man with prostate cancer metastases; daughter tearfully asks physician about father's condition; patient has stated he does not want family to know. HIPAA protects patient confidentiality: physician cannot disclose information to family without patient consent. Correct response: 'I can't discuss any information without his permission.'

47yo woman from Brazil, only elementary English; physician wants to discuss procedure; bilingual medical student offers to interpret. Federal law requires access to professional interpreter services at no cost. Family members and non-trained staff should NOT interpret. Use remote medical interpretation service (phone/video).

2mo boy with difficulty feeding, decreased arousability; mother says he 'rolled over and fell from bed'; purple discoloration at T4-T10, bilateral subdural hematomas. Shaken baby syndrome: rotational forces → tearing of bridging veins → subdural hematoma + retinal hemorrhages. Implausible history for injuries. Report to Child Protective Services.
